When I finally decided that it'd been sitting unplayed in my steam library long enough, I booted it up, & it was a fulfilling & surreal experience. It plays just like any Souls game. The aesthetic is beautiful, don't get turned off by it. There are three core weapon types & just as many primary playstyles: heavy, light, & ranged. I played light, prioritizing stabbing weapons that allowed one to do a light attack while still holding up their shield for protection. This let me stay relatively unharmed while attacking, assuming I could back off to recover stamina as needed. I also leveled up my ranged weapons, though I didn't use that as much. I used the heaviest armor & biggest shield I could find, though I leveled my carry capacity enough that it never slowed me down. Light weapons, ranged, carry weight, & stamina. I doubt the game was intended for a player to have as broad a focus of playstyle as I did, but I never I had to grind to cover so many stats. What helped was that I never once upgraded my health; I could use my stamina to absorb attacks with my shield while still attacking simultaneously. Did I have a cheap playstyle that carried me through the game? Possibly. But it was so much fun, & it certainly wasn't easy the whole way through. It was so satisfying to watch my real-world skills improve while playing; many times, I wouldn't know what stat to level up simply because I didn't feel like I needed to improve in any area. I've heard it said that this game is too hard at times, but safe to say I disagree & am baffled by the idea. There is a mechanic that allows you to summon ghosts to help you fight when you die, & it help with the difficulty where necessary. I have three bits of advice for new players: the amount of ghosts you can have depends on the amount of a certain type of item you have, this item is finite, find them all; don't feel like you shouldn't use ghosts, they're there for a reason, you don't have to fight everything yourself & you're not supposed to, the goal isn't to perform a solo genocide, it's to survive to the next "bonfire" any way that you can; & on occasional level-ups you'll get to learn a new ability, but these abilities aren't set in stone, you can change which abilities you're using in the menu at any time, don't hesitate to change it up if you're stuck.

This game doesn't have a fraction the amount of popularity & praise it deserves. Help me fix that, spread the word!

[b]Darkmaus[/b], actiony game, clean and simple.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
A light attack combo, a heavy attack, shielding and a dodge will be your bread and butter, but in true RPG fashion you’ll be able to access more options such as archery and magic to attack from afar, perks that will make your life easier and a stat allocation leveling system to build your character how you want.

The best addition to this game it’s the Shadow System, where in other games of the same type dying is a loss of progress, here when you die you’ll be followed by a shadow companion (or multiple shadow companions) who will fight along you until the spot of your death, making even failures feel like progress if you pushed your death spot far enough.

[h1]Story[/h1]
The story is very simple, there’s a mad king/necromancer, go kill him.

[h1]X-Factor[/h1]
Simplicity is it’s strongest asset, a generic RPG experience that is both functional and take you very little to complete, but has the same design philosophy of bigger titles.

Enemy AI tethers in the edge of good and broken, which is the best kind of AI since you can predict what it will do but still has that element of surprise to it.

[h1]Downsides[/h1]
Not many ways to approach the game, a variety build is the strongest, meaning there won’t be any other experimenting without severely handicapping your character.

The story abruptly ends, you fight someone that looks just like another boss or mini-boss and as soon as you defeat it the credits start rolling, no fanfare, no explanation, no nothing, it just... ends.
[hr][/hr]

A good starting point if you want to approach the genre for the first time, a short game that scratches your itch otherwise.

Soooo, I was wondering what I should do. Recommend, or not recommend? There's a lot of just, incredibly frustrating elements in this game I find, but I still enjoy it for the most part? And it has some.. curious systems I haven't seen in a game of its type before.

The whole game is basically "You arrive on a shore, assumedly from boat, and you're just kinda moving forward. Eventually you realise what you need to do, which is stop the big bad. So you fight yourway to the big bad, and either kill it or join it", but I do actually like some of the characters and what little bits of the story this game has to offer.

It is a short game, really short, actually. There's only about 1 area you /don't/ have to go through, and it's also the shortest area in the game if you do decide to go through it. I personally don't mind the length, though.


Naturally this game has STR weapons and DEX weapons. STR is stuff like "Longswords" Which are basically this games greatswords, and uh.. some other type of greatsword weapon that does crushing damage. They use a lot of stamina, swing slow, tend to hit hard and break guards real good. There's also just a one handed hammer with short range. Apparently it lowers enemy stamina per hit? I never noticed that, but it /does/ break a guard real good.

While im talking about breaking guards, want my advice? If you can catch a difficult enemy with their shield up and get their stamina all the way down? Keep pushing, and make your hits count. It is /very/ difficult to recover from losing your stamina in this game, and the AI will abuse that just as much as you will. And some of the AI enemies in this game are awful to fight but I'll get to that later.

The dex weapons, how about them? Shorter range, faster. That's the deal, basically. They aren't as good against guard breaking compared to strength weapons, but you have moves to get around that. There are attributes you can unlock and, thankfully, move those points around at any time!
Your first 3 points should go into the dodge sweep (so the game stops complaining you dont have it) and the next 2 into the skill that makes you dodge further, and makes you invulnerable while dodging. Yeah, that's a skill. And you will /need/ that skill. Thankfully the first lot of attribute points you get shower in!

There's also "Precision", precision is for ranged. Kinda. This stat affects bows and pyromancies. Keep in mind your str/dex/precision stat doesn't actually do anything other than let you use those weapons, not until you get it above 10. That's when you start getting increments of damage.

There is no replenishing healing item, either. Only consumables. I feel.. 50/50 about this. Most bosses can totally be beaten without healing items. On the other hand, this can make some sections incredibly frustrating. There's usually a campfire pretty close by, but I can find this frustrating as sometimes i just /want/ to power through a section and don't want to use the very low amoutn of healing items I find.
But, on the other hand, here's the reason why: Dying in this game spawns a.. shadow of sorts. Whatever your weapon was when you died, it will spawn with that weapon. These things are usually pretty solid, too, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ relentless.
Just don't die with a pyromancy flame out. They will kill themselves, you, and everything around it. Because pyromancy does friendly fire if you get yourself caught in the blast, and fire /♥♥♥♥♥♥♥/ hurts!

These shade fellows are a neat concept! I actually really like the idea the game is made /easier/ for those who die. And you can have 3/4 of these shades following you around?
... Though by the end of the game you'll need them, because it's the end game. And how did they make it difficult?
So, I'm gonna put it out here; i do NOT like AI fights where it's basically just a character with player abilities. Think of Red Phantom invaders from Dark Souls. Or Bloodborne.
The reason why I don't like this is because usually they make the phantoms tanky as ♥♥♥♥, and the phantoms do enough damage to kill you in 3/4 hits.
Same problem here. Except they also have better stamina. Better hit-stun resistance, and just.. yknow. And then they start making you fight 2 of them at the same time! That section is over really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fast, thankfully. And I don't think there's much that would stop you from just.. running straight through?

.. Speaking of which.. a spoilery section: [spoiler] there's.. interesting enemies you find. They're basically mirror fights, some of the time. They're like.. "Revenants" of your character? They usually give you really good ♥♥♥♥ if you can kill them, but they are hard to kill. They're ALL out of the way, sometimes hard to find, totally optional. You'll know them when you see them. [/spoiler]


Alright, this is the last thing I'll talk about before we get into spoilery sections. There isnt a lot of music in this game, but I like what music is present! I think it fits the mood well, and the whole atmosphere this game has is also.. very good. It's all kinda lonely, run down, etc. It's good.

Okay, spoiler section. If you care, avert thy eyes, but before you do, there is one bit of advice I wish to give you. I will spoiler this, in case you wish to have a FULLY blind playthrough. [spoiler] Don't give Destrain a morsel. He will help you through the 2nd half of the game, but just don't. Trust me. THis isn't even about how bad he is and how he will get himself downed all the time. [/spoiler]

 [spoiler] So two things. You know how I said I really don't like NPC fights that are like red phantoms from dark souls?
There's enemies in this game. Hunters. You'll know they're after you when the game music suddenly shifts to something foreboding, and you get the red text at the bottom "YOU ARE BEING HUNTED."
Hunters are scary. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They do a lot of damage, move fast, and are incredibly hard to pin down. If they kill you? Not only do they steal all of your marrow (your level up money), they also reduce your max health. They don't show up that often, and I think it may be timer based. So the faster you get through the game, the less hunters you'll see.

Now.. here's where we get to the last bit of that. The final boss is piss easy. It really can't do much to kill you.. so guess what the gimmick is?
That's right. At health thresholds it summons Hunters. Hunters can kill you in a few hits. They have a lot of health. They move fast, etc. And if you die, guess what? Max health loss. 
So you go back into the boss fight, without your shades because they don't WORK in boss fights, with even less health than you had before! I kinda hate that.
There.. is a but to that.

There's an NPC you can save, Destrain. Save him, but DON'T give him a morsel. Why? There's a lass you help out very early on. She's looking for her dad, so you look for her dad instead. Her dad is the 2nd final boss, a big monsterous thing with weird pincer like arms. Destrain will kill him after the boss fight in a fit of rage, locking you out of an item that prevents Hunters from stealing your Marrow but ONLY if that lass is alive. She won't give it to you if her dad dies, and she will take her own life shortly after.

And for the last bit.. You're given a choice by the big bad. "Join me or die", if you decide to join big bad, I think the game has you go back through all the areas you've been through and slay the last few living characters. There's maybe only about.. 5 or 6 of them. But I thought that was.. rather powerful and unique for a bad ending! Not often I've seen a game that makes you go back through and kill everyone to get the bad ending. [/spoiler]

So yeah! Those are all my thoughts on DarkMaus. It's a rather interesting souls-like. Unique in its own ways, though not without it's flaws. Still worth checking out as a curiousity.

I don't know what I can really say about this game. Another game in my catelog that I've had for years but never got around to completion (which is strange considering how quickly I finished up when I picked it back up in one night; it hasn't even been 2 hours since). The game is dark souls inspired if that wasn't clear but I'd say the game plays a bit different. Stamina regens slower, attacks have weight but i'm often left feeling like i'm too open after an attack, pyromancy seems to be greater in effectiveness here (it's also the only type of magic in the game), and there's no merchants of shops to buy items; most are obtained from enemies or loot.

I'd say the game has a bit of its own identity, but being familiar with dark souls will definitely help with how you play and go about some encounters. Bosses, though hard-hitting, can be cheesed if you're able to pick up on their attack "strategy" [spoiler] especially the next to last and last boss, but I'll get to that [/spoiler]. Enemies can be frustrating in groups and some encounters may seem outright unfair given what you may have and what you'll be up against, but I can assure you, most encounters can also be cheesed with relative security, if not without too much damage.

Since I'd been out of the loop for this game in years, I decided to try to watch a walkthrough to remember where I was as one of the game's main concerns for me is that your "quest", which is at the top right of the screen, is very vague. If you're playing continuously or in connected sessions, then you probably won't forget too much about where you are and where you're going, but I legitimately had no idea where I was, how I got there, and which way to go from there as it was at an intersection of possible paths to take. After realizing that the number of walkthroughs for the game that actually seem to beat it were not plentiful, I decided to throw caution to the wind and eventually I kind of stumbled upon where I was supposed to go.

Speaking of those walkthroughs, I noticed something in a number of them, even ones that had managed to get quite far, and it helps go into my next point. People just seem to get frustrated and decide, "I'll just run through this area and all it's enemies." And I don't think that's a bad play, but many of the areas in this game where (at least to me) that becomes your tactic, the enemies are placed in such a way as to negate that and in some cases, you are punished for it. Now far be it from me to tell someone not to ignore some fights; sometimes, you just have to in a game. But in the times I saw these mad dashes, the person is just taking unnecessary damage all to find the next campfire only to realize that they can't rest there because being actively engaged with enemies (who will some times follow you to the ends of the earth). That also means you have to disengage them completely, fight them all at once, or fight some enemies that wouldn't have been together in one setting to begin with.

This is not a smart plan. I get wanting to be done with something, but if you know that you face 3 separate rooms of enemies with 3 different types of fights to plan around, why would you actually want to group them all up so you fight them together? It seems like the enemy placement is setup in a way that you don't do this or you'll be punished. This is on top of the fact that there are NPC "invaders" called hunters who pop up at certain points in the game when you're exploring (you'll get a pop-up warning letting you know). You could potentially flag a bunch of heat on top of a hunter trailing after you, [spoiler] who, by the way, shares you're exact stats and sometimes build [/spoiler] and then get swarmed to death with no possible way of succeeding other than extreme luck. My advice? Fight some battles, avoid one's you think you can't handle. if you think you can't go one way because you're not sure how to take the fight ahead, do go until you've leveled up some more or gained some level of fortitude. Not bashing anyone, just saying I tried not to run through most fights because I'd be low on hp by the time I got to some safety and who knows what's behind the next corner?

A bit of a ramble there, but otherwise not much I found wrong with the combat aside for stamina regen being a bit too slow to me. As I said, most fights can be cheesed hard if you're smart about them; I had a good number of pyromancy spells and fireball was upgraded to hell (thanks a lot, past me) so whenever it seemed like I was up against a wall, the flames came out and would end the fight pretty quick. Another cheese is that most enemies, especially the more difficult to handle ones, seem to fold when you stick to them. This means an enemy with a fast lunging attack quickly becomes a joke when you're next to them wailing on them, because the lunge takes a lot of stamina and to dodge you would mean burning more so you stunlock them to death. This also works on you so running too much with eventually bite you in the back. Dodge when needed but be aggressive when you have no reason not to. Some bosses suffer from this "flaw" as well. [spoiler] The corrupted victor fight becomes a joke if you have timed block and a good one-handed sword. circle-strafing next to him while tapping timed block as he attacks means you barely if ever lose stamina and can attack him in his openings without worrying about his charging swipes. The last boss is even worst because you can kill his "help" before he calls them to his side. all three are on the sides of the arena, so run to one (which won't attack because they're not "summoned" yet) and just start hammering them to death before they have a chance to retaliate. When you finish all 3, the necromancer's call does absolutely nothing, so you can just circle-strafe and poke him until he's dead. [/spoiler]

Anyway, getting back into the game didn't take me too long, and I guess I must have stopped really far in the last time I play the game because I got the last boss fairly quick and beat him. Though I did die a couple of times here and there, most of the deaths we're me being a bit too brazen while being unaware of other enemies in the room. That's not to say there aren't any cheap deaths in the game, but they're not as often as they are made out to be. Overall, I think I enjoyed the game. If you're someone who plays a lot of Dark Souls or Dark Souls-esque games, I'm sure you'll enjoy this one. Anyone else may find their patience tested but I don't think it's that serious.

Played and finished the game back when it came out, decided to give it a go again years later. I remember now why I only gave the game one play-through: the game is brutal, and not in a fair or even fun way. 

Most areas after the very first beach feature extreme amounts of enemies that, while manageable, simply aren't fun to fight. Walls are sticky but only for the player (enemies tend to slide through corners that the player would collide with). Many fast weapons have comparable windup and wind-down to slow weapons. Enemies can attack and combo on empty stamina bars, and have a higher damage to stamina ratio than the player even after upgrading your gear and total stamina. This doesn't really matter since they can combo on empty anyway. Additionally, enemies with bigger weapons or unique animations swing and attack faster than the player in almost all instances. Increasing your swing speed early on is a complete waste that will gimp your future stats. I have been told that the game scales the difficulty. I can't attest to this, but it certainly feels like it.

My biggest gripe is that enemies are nearly or entirely unaffected by the wind. The wind seems to only work on the player, pushing you around and making it harder to go against its oncoming direction (it's the wind), which also reduces the distance you character will dodge if done into the wind. If you stand in the wind, pause your game, wait a bit and then unpause, you will be shot in the direction of the wind at high speed. If you sneak up behind a bull, you can see their feet vibrating, as if the wind should be pushing them. Obviously the wind can't push them because it would push them out of their spawn position or get them stuck on the edges of the map, but because of their wind immunity you are put at a serious movement disadvantage and get to enjoy a slog through pudding, sadness, and trees. Incidentally, enemies tend to get glitched and freeze in place anyway. I think that if dodge was unaffected by wind, this wouldn't be such a gripe for me, or if enemies were at least pushed by wind once aggro'd. No amount of scaling, bosses, enemies, traps, or other areas could compare to how painful the wind is alone. The plains area is so unfun that after I got through it this time around, I didn't feel like I needed or wanted to finish my final play-through.

Tras el éxito de Dark Souls, muchos juegos de jugabilidad similar o inspirados en el mismo aparecieron. Siendo este mi juego favorito me propuse recorrer estos títulos.
DarkMaus es otro de muchos.

Ambientación: 7.33/10
------------------------

* Historia. Si bien el juego empieza más simple imposible, pronto aparece una trama contada a través de los poco npc que vas encontrando. La historia es demasiado escueta como para explicarla brevemente sin dar spoilers. A pesar de ello, tiene su toque oscuro que le da un plus. 7/10
* Calidad Gráfica. Estamos hablando de un juego indie 2D con perspectiva aérea, así que no podemos pedir un acabado espectacular. Sin embargo, en base a esas limitaciones, creo que el juego ambienta bien cada zona distinta del juego. Quizás algunas zonas pueden liarte un poco por el semblante que tienen a otras, aunque por suerte hay un mapa. 7/10
* Música & Sonidos. Nada espectacular pero no por ello malo. Recuerda bastante a Dark Souls. 8/10
* Voces. No hay voces en este juego, pero tampoco le hacen falta. -/10


Jugabilidad: 8.5/10
---------------------

* Diversión. Diría que en términos de jugabilidad, por su dificultad y sensación que transmite es muy similar a Dark Souls. Si te lo pasas bien en Dark Souls y no te importa el cambio de perspectiva seguro que este juego te divertirá también. 9/10
* Controles. Unos controles muy similares a Dark Souls. 9/10
* Fluidez. El combate es muy fluido, puedes tomar distintas estrategias a la hora de enfrentarte a un mismo enemigo y cada una de ellas te dará su resultado en función de lo bien que las ejecutes. 9/10
* Rejugabilidad. Una vez terminas el juego empiezas NG+ inmediatamente con mayor dificultad. El ending del juego es bastante... pobre. 7/10


Aspectos Técnicos: 7.5/10
------------------------

* Claridad: El juego hace un buen trabajo explicando todos los conceptos y aquello que debes hacer. La única excepción sería que hay ocasiones en las que zonas ya exploradas quedan oscurecidas de nuevo en el mapa, dando lugar a confusión. No se si es un bug o simplemente funciona así. 8/10
* Interfaz: Una interfaz muy sencilla pero tampoco necesita mucho el juego. El mapa esta bien hecho pero tiene el problema mencionado anteriormente. 8/10
* Textos: Las conversaciones con los NPC son breves y no hay muchas, es bastante directa en la forma que se cuenta. 7/10
* Idioma: Exclusivamente en inglés, si solo sabes español puedes jugar igualmente pero te perderás la historia. 7/10


NOTA FINAL: 7.95/10

If you like Dark Souls, you'll probably like this game. It's pretty short and somewhat lacking in color palette, but for $10 it's definitely a recommend. It is true that the game kinda encourages you to kill yourself because doing so creates "ghost allies" that fight for you, but you have the option to turn them off, which in my experience makes the game feel a lot more like souls games than when they're enabled. The game also borrows the upgrade system of the souls games, so you can upgrade your favorite equipment and skills as you progress, ensuring you can always do enough damage to realistically slay your enemies (as long as you don't waste resources lol). Combat is weighty like the souls games, and there is a lot o fun to be had in figuring out what techniques work best against each of the enemies' techniques. Healing items are scarce, but it wasn't much of a problem for me, as you're supposed to play these games skillfully rather than by b1tchfighting. My biggest gripe is that you have a limited amount of time before your torch burns out and you have to refill it at a campfire, but campfires are way more plentiful in this game compared to bonfires in souls. If you like Dark Souls, you'll probably like DarkMaus.

Having spend only a limited amount of time in this game you should take this review with a grain of salt
Positive points
* beautiful art style that is both minimal and yet pleasing to the eye
* the shade system is an interesting mechanic
* as far as I have come the game appears to have an interesting world and lore
* The enemies are diverse and many act very differently, with the exception of the other mouse type of enemies many of whom mimic the PC in weapon choice and fighting style with the exception of having three times as much HP and doing many times the amount of damage the PC does.

Negative points
* The PC is extremely fragile compared to enemies and has infrequent access to healing items, even dark souls gave players automatically restoring healing items at every bonfire and because of this the gameplay suffers a little.
* Weapons are diverse but with finite upgrading material the game unintentionally discourages using weapons beyond those presented to you in the early game. Even further enforcing this is the unforgiving weight system which makes equipping two different weapons difficult if you also want to have a good dodge.
* The shade system actively encourages the player to suicide several times in order to get their shadows and be capable of advancing.
* The lack of guides that I could find makes advancing in this game harder than it should be

This is the best Souls-like apart from Nioh. 

We live in a time where sword&magic games are becoming just about clicking the attack button. Games like The Witcher 3, Nier Automata, Devil May Cry and Skyrim are almost just about smashing the attack and heal buttons, yet get astonishing reviews, both from critics and fans.
This is why the Dark Souls has become so important, because it made developers stop being lazy. No, pretty graphics and a decent story isn't enough. A game isn't just a movie. A game must have some challenge, otherwise it isn't a game!

DarkMaus 100% excells in this, giving you a very rewarding and challenging combat. (not necessarily difficult)
It also completely excells in the other aspect which made the Souls genre stand-out: the immersive dark atmosphere.
That's why, in my opinion, it's the best Souls like, apart from Nioh, the only big-budget Souls-like to date.
